series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

derived.$note: Trend: least-squares slope over 35 observed years (1990-2024) from DS-35, compared against the DS-06-NDC-LATEST target of 9.263 MtCO₂e by 2030. The two are not necessarily on the same inventory scope, see series.$note. The target tonnage is derived here, not quoted: 47% below DS-35's 1990 value of 17.478 MtCO₂e. The document states the percentage; the level it is applied to comes from DS-35, on DS-35's inventory scope, which is not necessarily the document's.
derived.$reason: observed emissions are rising by 0.03 MtCO₂e/yr while the target requires a fall of 0.53 MtCO₂e/yr. No multiple of the current trend reaches it, so no finite gap factor is reported.

target_text.text: Georgia is fully committed to an unconditional target to reduce its domestic GHG emissions by 35% below 1990 levels by 2030, excluding LULUCF emissions/removals. This goal translates to a maximum emissions level of 29,250 Gg of CO₂ eq. by 2030. The target is supported through domestically implemented mitigation measures and policies. Georgia is committed to a conditional target to reduce its total GHG emissions by 50-57% below 1990 levels by 2030 (excluding LULUCF emissions/removals), contingent upon international support. Achieving a 50% reduction aligns with a global pathway to limit warming to 2°C, translating to a maximum emissions level of 23,300 Gg CO₂ eq. To limit warming to 1.5°C, a 57% reduction would be required, capping emissions at 20,300 Gg CO₂ eq. by 2030.

verdict.text: Georgia pledges a 47% reduction by 2030 against 1990 baseline (condition not read). The registry's current submission for this Party is NDC 3.0, filed 2026-03-25. 69 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (23). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-02 21.4 MtCO₂e, DS-35 12.4 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. The target is not reached on the observed trend. Both figures are on DS-35's inventory: the document's percentage applied to DS-35's 1990 level, not the document's own. It submitted BTR1. 4 of 8 components have been confirmed in the document; the rest are unparsed, which is not a finding against the country. ND-GAIN scores it 55.3 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: 15% (unconditional) to 25% (conditional) reduction in GHG emissions for the year 2030 compared to the BAU scenario It was classed both. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +1.56°C under SSP1-2.6 to +5.54°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
